FACTUAL MATRIX- 1.

The facts which led to the present case are that upon receiving secret information that two persons (the accused herein) were committing cheating by pretending to sell real mobile phone, receiving money in lieu thereof but actually providing a piece of mirror instead, ASI Rampal created a raiding team consisting of Ct. Rajesh, Ct. Anil and himself.
They went to Service Road, near Sriram Sharnam Mandir, Lajpat Nagar-IV where the secret informer pointed towards two persons standing near a motorcycle as the persons who were committing cheating.

Thereafter, ASI Ram Pal gave a Rs.

1 500 note to Ct. Rajesh and sent him as a decoy customer.

After some time, Ct. Rajesh gave the agreed upon signal to show that the persons were committing cheating and the said persons tried to flee on their motorcycle however they were caught by the raiding team.

2. As such, it is alleged that the accused persons committed the offence punishable under section 420 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC") for which FIR No. 509/2017 was registered at Police Station Amar Colony, New Delhi.

sentences.text: INVESTIGATION AND APPEARANCE OF ACCUSED- 3.

After registration of the FIR, the Investigating Officer (hereinafter, "IO") undertook investigation and arrested the accused persons and on culmination of the same, the charge-sheet against the accused persons was filed.

After taking cognizance of the offence, the accused persons were summoned to face trial vide order dated 05.03.2019.
4.
On their appearance, a copy of charge-sheet was supplied to the accused persons in terms of Section 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, "CrPC").
On finding a prima facie case against the accused persons, charge under Section 420/34 IPC was framed against them.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
PROSECUTION EVIDENCE- 5.
During the trial, the prosecution examined three witnesses to prove its case against the accused persons.
All the witnesses relevant to the case have been examined and cross- examined.
6. Ct. Rajesh (PW-1) deposed that on 06.11.2017 he was posted as Constable at PS Amar Colony and at about 7:30 p.m.
IO ASI Rampal received information from secret informer regarding cheating by done by the two accused persons by showing original mobile phone but giving fake mobile phone instead.
He along with ASI Rampal and Ct. Anil went to Sri Ram Mandir, Service Road, Lajpat Nagar, IV where they met the secret informer.
Thereafter, the secret informer pointed out towards two persons who were standing near motorcycle and said that these were the persons who sell fake mobile and informer left the spot.

IO gave a note of Rs. 500/- bearing number 2QF645852 to Ct.
Rajesh and asked him to approach the two accused to try to purchase a mobile phone from them and in case he suspected anything, to give a signal by patting his hand on his head.

When PW-1 approached the two accused, they said Rs. 500 is a meagre amount to buy a mobile phone but finally agreed to sell the same for the same amount and gave him a black box but when he checked the box,
a piece of glass was found therein.
PW-1 gave signal to IO and Ct. Amit by patting on his head and they caught the accused persons when they were trying to escape on their motorcycle Apache bearing no. UP 14 CS 3670.
He deposed that IO made inquiry from the accused persons.
PW-1 deposed that he told the IO that the Rs. 500 note was kept in the right-side pocket of accused Sajid upon which IO seized the same from his pocket.
He further stated that IO prepared rukka at 8:45 p.m. and gave the same to Ct. Anil for registration of FIR.
Ct. Anil got the FIR registered and returned to the spot along with copy of FIR and original rukka and handed over the same to the IO.

PW1 deposed that IO seized the Rs. 500 note from accused Sajid, 2 boxes containing a piece of glass and one Motorola mobile phone from accused Rupesh and one motorcycle from both the accused State vs Sajid on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109964528/
2 which are Ex. PW1/1 to Ex. PW1/5 respectively.

IO prepared the Site plan, arrested the accused persons (arrest memos being Ex. PW1/8 and Ex, PW1/9 respectively) and conducted their personal search, the memos being Ex. PW1/6 and PW1/7 respectively.
Thereafter PW1 and Ct. Anil took the accused persons for medical examination and then to the police station.
The witness correctly identified the accused persons as well as the case property.
6.1 PW1 was cross examined by the defence counsel wherein PW1 stated that at the time of incident there was no mobile phone which was available for purchase for Rs. 500/-in the market.
It was revealed that there was no previous complaint against the accused regarding involvement in case of cheating.
Accused Rupesh was carrying mobile boxes in his pocket.
All documents were prepared at the spot which PW-1 left at about 11:00 to 11:30 p.m.
He denied contrary suggestions put forth on behalf of the accused.

7. HC Anil (PW-2) deposed in his examination that he accompanied ASI Ram Pal on a raid on 06.11.2017 near Shri Ram Sharnam Mandir, Lajpat Nagar-I, New Delhi and ASI Rampal had sent Ct.
Rajesh to the two persons who were cheating by showing real mobile phones but selling pieces of glass instead at Service Road, Ring Road, Lajpat Nagar-IV.
He further stated that Ct. Rajesh gave the signal as told by IO and in the meanwhile the accused persons started fleeing away on a motorcycle however he and IO chased them and caught hold of them.
He narrated the steps taken thereafter as narrated by PW1.
He also deposed that IO recorded disclosure statement of accused Sajid and Rupesh (Ex. PW2/1 and Ex. PW2/2 respectively).
The witness correctly identified the accused persons as well as the case property.
7.1 PW2 was cross examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused persons where he stated that they reached the spot from the police station within 5 minutes.
The distance between the PS and the spot was 1-1.5 km.
Accused persons were 500 metres away from Shri Ram Sharnam Mandir.
Accused persons were selling Motorola mobile phone for Rs. 500.
He denied contrary suggestions.
8. ASI Ram Pal Singh/PW-3 is the IO.

He deposed on oath that on 06.11.2017 at about 6:45 p.m., he received information from secret informer regarding committing of cheating, i.e., by showing original mobile phone to customers, seller gives fake mobile.
He narrated the same story as PW1 and PW2.
He also added that he asked 4-5 persons to join the investigation but none of the m agreed to join the same.

He then narrated the conversation which took place between Ct. Rajesh and the accused persons regarding the mobile phone as told to him by Ct. Rajesh and also deposed as to the steps taken by him in the investigation as already told by PW1 and PW2.
PW3 also proved the tehrir (Ex. PW3/1) and site plan (Ex. PW3/2).

He also recorded statements under section 161 CrPC of Ct.
Rajesh and Ct. Anil.
The witness correctly identified the accused persons as well as the case property.
8.1 PW3 was cross examined by the ld. defence Counsel.
It was revealed that the IO had never received information regarding cheating at the place of incident prior to the present case.
He was carrying the IO kit at the time of raid.
They had gone to the spot on foot.
The distance between the PS and the spot was 500-700 metres.
It took 5 hours to complete the investigation.
They came to the spot at about 7:00-7:15 p.m. and Ct. Anil took the tehrir at PS at about 8:00-8:30 p.m.

He denied State vs Sajid on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109964528/
3 contrary suggestions put forth on behalf of the accused persons.

The accused persons admitted the genuineness (without contents) of FIR registered in the present case (Ex. A-1), DD entry no. 37A dated 06.11.2017 (Ex. A-2), DD entry no. 38A dated 06.11.2017 (Ex.
A-3) and DD entry no. 43A dated 06.11.2017 (Ex. A-4).
Therefore, formal examination of witnesses to prove the aforesaid documents was dispensed with under section 294 CrPC. STATEMENT OF ACCUSED AND DEFENCE EVIDENCE - 10.

Thereafter, to enable the accused persons to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against them, the statement of the accused persons was recorded without oath under Section 313(1)(b) CrPC wherein they denied the incriminating evidence appearing against them except the admitted documents and stated that they have been falsely implicated.
They also stated that the witnesses have deposed against them because they are interested witnesses.

Accused Sajid also stated that he was returning home from his maternal uncle's house and stopped on the way for some snacks at a place near Ram Sharnam Temple but was not selling any phones at that place.

Accused Rupesh added that he was standing at Ram Mandir and smoking when the police official arrested him and that he was not selling any phone at that place.
11.
Pursuant thereto, the accused persons chose not to lead defence evidence.
Thus, the matter was fixed for final arguments.
Arguments of both sides were heard at length and the record has been perused carefully.
ARGUMENTS -
12. Ld. APP for the State argued that all the ingredients of the offences are fulfilled in the present case.
He submitted that the accused persons used to show a real phone but deliver other things instead such as piece of glass therefore a team was made to catch them.
Ct. Rajesh who was the decoy customer bought a phone for Rs. 500/- but when he opened the box, a piece of glass was found therein therefore the accused persons were caught.
He also submitted that the fact that a phone was recovered from Rupesh and two more boxed with glass were recovered shows the intent and modus operandi of the accused persons.

It was argued that all the essential ingredients, i.e.,
inducement, dishonest intention and delivery of property, are fulfilled in the present case.
He referred to all the witnesses and contended that their testimonies are consistent and identity as well as documentary evidence is not disputed by the defence.
Thus, it is prayed that the accused persons be convicted for the said offences.
13. Per contra, learned counsel for the accused persons contended that the State has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.

He pointed out that no mobile phone is worth Rs. 500 therefore the story of the prosecution is flawed that the accused persons were selling a phone for Rs.
500.
He also contended that no public witnesses were examined despite the area being crowded.

It was also argued that there is no record of glass being sold instead of phone to any other customer/witness therefore it is a false case against the accused persons who have no such previous involvement.
As such, it is prayed that the accused deserve to be acquitted of the said offence.

4 INGREDIENTS OF THE OFFENCE 14.
Before dwelling into the facts of the present case, it would be apt to discuss the legal standards required to be met by both sides.
In criminal law, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused exclusively lies on the prosecution which must prove the offences charged beyond reasonable doubt.
The benefit of doubt, if any, must go in favour of the accused.

15. Section 420 IPC punishes cheating and thereby dishonestly inducing the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security.

Cheating is defined under section 415 IPC as follows - whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived,
and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind,
reputation or property, is said to "cheat".
Section 34 IPC fixes vicarious liability upon persons committing an offence with common intention.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE - 16.

The case of the prosecution is that on 06.11.2017 at about 7:00 p.m. the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention cheated the complainant Ct. Rajesh Kumar at Shri Ram Sharnam Mandir by giving him a black plastic like pouch containing a piece of glass on the pretext of selling a mobile phone.
The identity and presence of the accused at the spot at the given time and place are not in dispute.
17. As per the prosecution version, the accused persons were caught in a raid on the basis of information given by secret informer.
The prosecution witnesses have failed to prove how the information reached them based on which the raid was conducted.
Of course, the said informer was not examined as a witness.
However, the case of the prosecution is dubious as it has not been able to show any efforts to join even a single independent witness in the investigation and recovery.

18. In Bhal Singh v. The State AIR1960P&H641 conviction was set aside and it was held that "there ought to be some extraneous material wholly independent of the police mechanization to show that the sale in question was pushed by the petitioner of the spurious cycle parts representing them to be genuine of "Hercules" or "Phillips" makes.

entities.text: Bhal Singh v. The State AIR1960P&H641 conviction
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This material is lacking."
19.
In the present case, the only witnesses are police witnesses.
PW3 cursorily stated that he asked 4-5 persons to join the investigation but they did not join.
He has not given any notice to these persons, nor noted their names and addresses.
Thus, sufficient efforts were not made to ensure inclusion of independent witnesses in investigation and recovery procedure.
Similarly, no photographs of the spot were taken and no videography of the raid was conducted.
The aforesaid circumstances cast a grave doubt on the prosecution case.

State vs Sajid on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109964528/
5 20.

The offence under section 420 IPC requires that an inducement is made and pursuant thereto,
the person so cheated part with some valuable property which cause wrongful loss to him &
wrongful gain to the others.
In the present case, there the complainant was trying to entrap the accused persons; therefore, he cannot be said to have been induced by the accused persons to part with Rs. 500.
There is no evidence on record of any prior customer/victim who complained that they have been cheated by the accused persons in this modus operandi.
Therefore, all the ingredients of the offence are also not made out.
21. It is also unlikely that the accused persons were selling mobile phones in boxes from their pockets for Rs. 500/- on the roadside.

Furthermore, PW-3's deposition regarding what transpired during the purchase transaction between the accused persons and PW-1 does not lend credence to the prosecution case as it is in the nature of hearsay and PW-1 has not deposed to the said facts though he was examined as a witness.
22. Summing up, to bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution was required to prove the offence charged against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.

Prosecution witnesses have not been able to fully establish the circumstances against the accused persons, there is not even a single independent witness and even the inducement aspect of the offence has not been established.
Hence, the benefit of the doubt must go in favour of the accused persons.
CONCLUSION - 23.
Resultantly, accused Sajid and Rupesh Kumar are ACQUITTED for the offences under section 420/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Pronounced in open court on 14.05.2024 This judgment comprises of 11 signed pages.
(NEHA BARUPAL) Metropolitan Magistrate - 12 South-East District, Saket Courts, New Delhi/14.05.2024
